raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Give each rank its own CPU region outside the replicated layout, using logical worker ranks consistently with #58497. Count per-rank page padding against the full CPU budget and check aggregate shared-memory and cgroup headroom before any rank allocates. Capacity failures still release workers waiting at the readiness barrier. Replicated CPU regions and the tiered offloader retain their shared layouts.

## Tests

- Current source `9cff68d835`, 1× NVIDIA H100 80GB: 194 factory, shared-region, capacity and GPU worker tests passed; 5 ROCm-only tests skipped.
- With the previous CPU spec source (`980cf33256`), the focused capacity regressions produced 4 failures and 3 passes; the updated source passes all 7 cases.
- An injected capacity failure on `5303672870` reproduced the missing readiness barrier; the updated regression passes and preserves the capacity error.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

Historical validation on 4× H200, using `16d4ac4ba3` with the original per-rank change:

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: startup fell from 63.6 to 22.6 s (22.8 and 22.4 s in two runs), and pinning from 20.8 to 3.3 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- The broader offloading and worker suite passed 1,182 tests. Seven tests required a gated model and failed the same way on that run's main baseline.

nodes.body:
While studying the performance optimizations in [#59544](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59544)–[#59547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59547), I was inspired to open [#60782](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60782).

The different shared-region paths make view, populate, and pin ownership harder to maintain, and their ranges are not always aligned. #60782 is a behavior-preserving refactor that gives each caller an explicit region implementation and keeps these operations together.

It does not change the current ranges or barrier behavior. I’d appreciate thoughts on whether this structure could provide a cleaner foundation for optimizations like yours.

cc @robertgshaw2-redhat @Etelis

nodes.body:
Claude:
    the /dev/shm and cgroup capacity check now
    under-detects by a factor of world_size. `SharedOffloadRegion` calls
    `check_shm_free_space(self.total_size_bytes)` on the creator path
    (shared_offload_region.py:137). Before, exactly one creator checked the full
    `cpu_bytes_to_use`. Now all world_size ranks are creators and each checks
    `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size`.
    Concrete: `--shm-size=128g`, `cpu_bytes_to_use=256GiB`, TP4. Before: the creator sees
    256 GiB required > 128 GiB free and raises the intended RuntimeError
    ("Increase /dev/shm…") at startup. After: each rank sees 64 GiB ≤ 128 GiB free — all
    four pass, because they race on the same free-space snapshot and tmpfs `ftruncate` is
    sparse so nothing is charged yet — and the failure resurfaces as ENOSPC or SIGBUS
    inside `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`/the fallback page-touch loop, mid-startup, with no
    actionable message. `check_cgroup_memory_available` degrades the same way.
    Fix: check the aggregate once — pass a `creator_memory_check` validating
    `total_size_bytes * world_size`, or keep one designated rank checking the full budget.

nodes.body:
Claude:
    aggregate /dev/shm can exceed
    `cpu_bytes_to_use`. `num_chunks` is still derived (spec.py:116-119) from
    `round_up(world_size * p, PAGESIZE)`, but each rank now reserves
    `num_chunks * round_up(p, PAGESIZE)`. Padding moved from once per chunk row to once per
    rank per row, so the aggregate is `num_chunks * world_size * round_up(p)` and overshoots
    by up to `num_chunks * (world_size - 1) * PAGESIZE`.
    Concrete: MLA-shaped per-worker pages are routinely not page-aligned (e.g. 576 latent
    dims × 2 B × block_size 16 = 18432 B per layer, ×61 layers = 1,124,352 B = 274.5 pages).
    At 256 GiB with ~4 MiB chunks (~65k chunks) and TP4 that is ~0.8 GiB over budget — small
    in absolute terms, but it silently breaks the "`cpu_bytes_to_use` is a budget" contract
    and grows with world_size.
    Fix: recompute `num_chunks` from the per-rank row size,
    `cpu_bytes_to_use // (world_size * round_up(p, PAGESIZE))`, when not replicated.

nodes.body: Left a couple of unverified Claude comments.

Claude:
The region calls `creator_memory_check` only on the creator branch (`shared_offload_region.py:165-166`).
Joiners and creators that fail before line 166 call the `lambda: None` instead, so the remaining ranks sit in the collective until `default_pg_timeout`.
The fix is to stop needing a collective: check the aggregate where every rank arrives unconditionally.

nodes.body:
Only node-local ranks allocate in a given `/dev/shm`, and multi-node non-replicated is reachable (`replicated_layout` requires `nnodes_within_dp == 1`).
2 nodes × TP4 at 256 GiB with `--shm-size=140g` fits at 128 GiB per node but gets refused.
Plumb `local_world_size` through `OffloadingParallelConfig` and use it as the multiplier, so multi-node TP is not rejected for memory it never allocates.

Claude:
    the /dev/shm and cgroup capacity check now
    under-detects by a factor of world_size. `SharedOffloadRegion` calls
    `check_shm_free_space(self.total_size_bytes)` on the creator path
    (shared_offload_region.py:137). Before, exactly one creator checked the full
    `cpu_bytes_to_use`. Now all world_size ranks are creators and each checks
    `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size`.
    Concrete: `--shm-size=128g`, `cpu_bytes_to_use=256GiB`, TP4. Before: the creator sees
    256 GiB required > 128 GiB free and raises the intended RuntimeError
    ("Increase /dev/shm…") at startup. After: each rank sees 64 GiB ≤ 128 GiB free — all
    four pass, because they race on the same free-space snapshot and tmpfs `ftruncate` is
    sparse so nothing is charged yet — and the failure resurfaces as ENOSPC or SIGBUS
    inside `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`/the fallback page-touch loop, mid-startup, with no
    actionable message. `check_cgroup_memory_available` degrades the same way.
    Fix: check the aggregate once — pass a `creator_memory_check` validating
    `total_size_bytes * world_size`, or keep one designated rank checking the full budget.

Claude:
    aggregate /dev/shm can exceed
    `cpu_bytes_to_use`. `num_chunks` is still derived (spec.py:116-119) from
    `round_up(world_size * p, PAGESIZE)`, but each rank now reserves
    `num_chunks * round_up(p, PAGESIZE)`. Padding moved from once per chunk row to once per
    rank per row, so the aggregate is `num_chunks * world_size * round_up(p)` and overshoots
    by up to `num_chunks * (world_size - 1) * PAGESIZE`.
    Concrete: MLA-shaped per-worker pages are routinely not page-aligned (e.g. 576 latent
    dims × 2 B × block_size 16 = 18432 B per layer, ×61 layers = 1,124,352 B = 274.5 pages).
    At 256 GiB with ~4 MiB chunks (~65k chunks) and TP4 that is ~0.8 GiB over budget — small
    in absolute terms, but it silently breaks the "`cpu_bytes_to_use` is a budget" contract
    and grows with world_size.
    Fix: recompute `num_chunks` from the per-rank row size,
    `cpu_bytes_to_use // (world_size * round_up(p, PAGESIZE))`, when not replicated.

issue_comments.body:
While studying the performance optimizations in [#59544](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59544)–[#59547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59547), I was inspired to open [#60782](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60782).

The different shared-region paths make view, populate, and pin ownership harder to maintain, and their ranges are not always aligned. #60782 is a behavior-preserving refactor that gives each caller an explicit region implementation and keeps these operations together.

It does not change the current ranges or barrier behavior. I’d appreciate thoughts on whether this structure could provide a cleaner foundation for optimizations like yours.
